thread:
maya: Heads-up: we saw an anomaly in the fncall strict-validate canary this morning. Rejects jumped to ~5% for rwd-cpu:canary around 07:08 UTC. Posting here for triage.
jon: Do we have error types? schema_mismatch or parse_error? Any model_variant pattern?
lucy: Console trace shows repeated "schema_mismatch: expected object, got array" from fncall validator. Samples are tiny like ["done"]. Happens only on canary variant rwd-cpu:canary-2026-03.
telemetry-bot: Alert: fncall_validation_rejects > 4% (5m) route=/v1/invoke region=us-west-2 variant=rwd-cpu:canary-2026-03
maya: Key questions: 1) revert canary vs 2) fallback reroute to permissive path vs 3) temporary accounting exclusion for canary windows. Thoughts?
jon: Revert is simplest and least risky for customers. But we lose canary signal. Fallback reroute would keep the signal but we need to resolve billing attribution.
lucy: If we transparently reroute to permissive, the billing system currently attributes tokens to the original routing policy (strict). finance-bot: FYI: any request that flows through strict-validate tagging increments strict_variant cost buckets. There's no separate metric for rerouted requests today.
finance-bot: Proposal: add a route_tag header when router rewrites the path (eg x-rw-route-tag: "permissive-fallback") and have billing ingest map that tag to permissive buckets. That requires a 2-day schema change and backfill plan.
sre-oncall: For immediate mitigation I recommend: pause canary; add sampling of failing requests; and create a dashboard tile showing rejects by variant with links to samples. Then plan the billing header change.
maya: Agreed. Action plan: 1) lucy -> start sample pipeline for 300 fails with scrubber, 2) jon -> pause canary slice, 3) telemetry-bot -> create dashboard tile "fncall rejects by variant (sample links)", 4) finance-bot -> draft billing header schema spec.
lucy: Starting sampling now. Samples written to s3://redwood-temp/canary-samples/1755559999/ with TTL=168h. Scrubber removed potentially sensitive tokens and email-like patterns.
jon: Pausing canary slice (10% traffic) now. Reverting traffic to rwd-cpu:stable-2026-02. Monitoring for fallout.
telemetry-bot: Dashboard panel created: fncall rejects by variant (5m). Linked sample store. Panel ID: dash-1729.
finance-bot: Draft spec for x-rw-route-tag submitted: https://git.internal/redwood/billing/pulls/324. Notes: header must be set by router only, immutable downstream. Backfill requires a mapping table.
maya: Two follow-ups: A) we should prevent automatic reject-accounting alerts from firing for canary windows (unless the canary is deliberate). B) add a short-lived flag in console to ignore canary-window validation counts for billing notifications.
jon: We can implement an internal flag that suppresses notify rules and accounting only for slices tagged as "canary-pause-safe". But we need audit logs. I'll open ENG-2102.
lucy: Research team asked for a tiny repro harness. I'll include 200 of the scrubbed prompts in the sample bundle and hand off to model owners.
sre-oncall: Observability note: while paused, we might still see residual rejects from older requests. Keep an eye on the 95th p90 latency but no KV-cache mismatch is expected (caches are per-variant).
maya: Monitoring shows rejects dropping back to baseline. Good. We'll keep canary paused until model team confirms output contract compatibility and we have the billing header spec.
jon: Post-mortem owners: model-team + eng-platform. I'll tag ENG-2102 with required checks: schema-compat-unit-tests, integration test with validator, and canary smoke test.
telemetry-bot: Reminder: schedule a 1h sync with billing and eng-platform to finalize header mapping and dashboard changes. Proposed slot tomorrow 1500 UTC.
maya: Thanks all. Closing the immediate incident. Please file follow-ups in ENG-2102 and mark samples as sensitive-handling. :thumbsup:
